reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about surface-energy-driven segregation, diffusivity-enabled segregation, short-range order formation, and their effect on melting onset in a complex HEA nanoparticle system, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific segregation and melting behavior of this five-component HEA nanoparticle composition, so the lack of cited support leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: Differences in constituent surface energies drive local chemical segregation at nanoparticle surfaces
Differences in atomic diffusivities enable local chemical segregation
Local chemical segregation produces nanoscale regions of short-range order
These segregated regions lower the effective melting onset compared to a homogeneous solid solution
Annealing can minimize pre-existing surface segregation in HEA nanoparticles
